statement: The Latin alphabet derives from Greek, transmitted via the Etruscan alphabet (itself imported from Euboean Greek colonies at Cumae/Ischia in the Gulf of Naples, 8th century BCE; archaeological support includes the 1957-58 Veii excavations by the British School at Rome showing Cumae/Ischia contact from the mid-8th century BCE). Whether Latin's direct source is Etruscan intermediation or a more direct Cumaean-Greek borrowing bypassing Etruscan is a genuine, documented, unresolved scholarly dispute — both positions are live in the literature.
scholarly_disagreement: Etruscan-mediated transmission vs. direct Cumaean-Greek borrowing bypassing Etruscan — both positions live, no clear majority signal found in this research pass.

sources.citation: British School at Rome, Veii excavation reports, 1957-58.
General epigraphic literature on the Etruscan-vs-direct-Greek transmission dispute for Latin.
